title: Match your experience to the jobs worth pursuing | SearchBreaker
description: See where your experience meets a job’s requirements before spending time applying. Learn the workflow, its controls and what you can review before applying.

blocks.headline: Match your experience to the jobs worth pursuing
blocks.lead: Paste or select a job and SearchBreaker compares its requirements with the experience you confirmed. You see what is supported, what is missing and what is unclear, then decide whether to apply.

media.label: Requirement breakdown
media.alt: Example of job requirements mapped to confirmed evidence with a status for each
media.caption: Every requirement shows the evidence behind its status.

blocks.reassurance: No score replaces your own judgment.

blocks.heading: See your fit for a specific role
blocks.lead: Each requirement is marked supported, partial, a gap or unclear, with the evidence from your profile beside it.

blocks.heading: How the match is explained
blocks.lead: The match shows its reasoning instead of hiding it behind a number.

items.title: Requirements from the job
items.text: The posting is broken into separate requirements you can read one by one.

items.title: Evidence from your profile
items.text: Each requirement is compared only with facts you confirmed, never with guesses.

items.title: A status you can check
items.text: Supported, partial, gap or unclear, so you can correct a misread or fill a gap.

blocks.heading: Decide: apply, improve or skip
blocks.lead: The breakdown ends in a decision that stays with you.

points.title: Apply with the right resume
points.text: When the evidence is strong, pick the base resume that fits best and move on to tailoring.

points.title: Improve your profile first
points.text: If a gap is real experience you left out, add it and check the match again.

points.title: Skip and move on
points.text: If the gaps are real, skip the job and spend the time on a better fit.

blocks.heading: Match score limitations
blocks.lead: A match shows how your confirmed experience lines up with a job description. It is a decision aid, not a forecast.

items.title: It does not predict interviews
items.text: Hiring decisions depend on people and on factors that are not in the job text.

items.title: It only sees what you entered
items.text: Experience missing from your profile lowers the match, even if you have it.

items.title: Job descriptions are incomplete
items.text: Many requirements are unstated or flexible. The match cannot see them.

items.title: It is not an ATS result
items.text: Employers configure their systems differently. No outside tool can replicate them.

faqs.a: No. It reflects how your confirmed facts line up with the text of one job. Two people can read the same posting differently, so the reasoning is shown rather than hidden.
No. A requirement with no matching fact is marked as a gap. It is never filled in for you.
No. The match does not estimate your chance of an interview and does not claim to.

faqs.q: How is this different from an ATS score?
faqs.a: An ATS score is about how a resume is read by a system. The match is about how your experience lines up with a job’s requirements.

faqs.q: Is the job matcher available now?
faqs.a: It is in private testing. Join the waitlist to get an invite.
